description: Single-panel pseudo-binary equilibrium phase diagram, calculated by Thermo-Calc with the TCFE9 database for the Fe-7.95Mn-0.25C-4.94Al (wt.%) steel. The x-axis is "Weight Percent of Al", 0-10 with 1 wt.% ticks; the y-axis is "Temperature (°C)", 500-1600 with 100 °C ticks. Labelled phase fields, top to bottom: L; a narrow γ+L wedge arrowed near 0-1 wt.% Al at ~1450 °C; α+L across the upper right; a large γ field on the left; γ+α on the right; γ+θ below a blue solvus at ~530-620 °C on the left; a small γ+α+κ pocket near 5-6.5 wt.% Al at ~600 °C; α+κ to the right, with additional brown/orange κ-type boundary curves running down toward 8-10 wt.% Al and ~600-900 °C. Boundaries are thin black, blue and orange curves. A red "Current Study" annotation marks the alloy composition: a dashed red horizontal line at the 850 °C gridline runs from the y-axis to a dashed red vertical line at just under the 5 wt.% Al gridline (consistent with the 4.94 wt.% Al stated in the caption), which drops to the x-axis with an upward-pointing arrowhead. The diagram therefore demonstrates that at 850 °C this alloy sits inside the γ+α two-phase field, i.e. its Al content stabilises ferrite.

observations.observation: The plot axes are labelled 'Temperature (°C)' (500-1600, 100 °C ticks) and 'Weight Percent of Al' (0-10, 1 wt.% ticks).
Phase fields labelled in the diagram are L, γ+L, α+L, γ, γ+α, γ+θ, γ+α+κ and α+κ.

A red annotation 'Current Study' consists of a dashed red horizontal line lying on the 850 °C gridline, running from the y-axis to a dashed red vertical line at just below the 5 wt.% Al gridline that drops to the x-axis with an upward arrowhead.
The composition/temperature point marked by the red dashed lines falls inside the field labelled γ+α, to the right of the γ single-phase field boundary.

At low Al contents the region below a blue boundary curve at roughly 530-620 °C is labelled γ+θ, while a small pocket labelled γ+α+κ lies between about 5 and 6.5 wt.% Al near 600 °C, and α+κ lies further right.
Additional brown/orange phase-boundary curves descend through the right-hand part of the diagram (roughly 7-10 wt.% Al, 600-900 °C) without a printed phase label for every enclosed region.
No δ symbol appears in the diagram: the high-temperature ferrite-bearing field is labelled α+L and the lower one γ+α, so the figure itself does not print the term δ-ferrite.
The figure is a pseudo-binary equilibrium phase diagram for Fe-7.95Mn-0.25C-4.94Al (wt.%) calculated with Thermo-Calc using the TCFE9 database.
The cited text states that the Al addition 'promotes the formation of δ-ferrite, as illustrated by the phase diagram shown in Fig. 1'.
The cited text gives the alloy density as ~7.40 g/cm3 and states the Al addition reduced density by 6.2%.
The cited text states the cold-rolled sheet was intercritically annealed at 850 °C for 10 minutes followed by water quenching, matching the 850 °C red dashed line in the diagram.
The cited processing sequence is vacuum induction melting, homogenisation at 1100 °C, hot rolling to ~3 mm above ~1000 °C, then cold rolling to ~1.5 mm.

unreadable_items: The exact numerical value of the red vertical dashed line is not printed on the figure; it is read only as lying just below the 5 wt.% Al gridline (the caption gives 4.94 wt.% Al).

Several boundary curves in the right-hand part of the diagram (about 7-10 wt.% Al) are drawn without printed phase-field labels, so the identity of those narrow fields cannot be confirmed from the pixels.
